sources.entry: LocalAI - Run your AI models locally and generate images and audio (alternative to OpenAI and Claude). (Source Code, Clients) MIT Docker/K8S
LocalAI | Drop-in OpenAI API replacement for running LLMs, image and audio models on your own hardware

summary.one_liner: LocalAI is an open-source, self-hostable OpenAI/Anthropic/ElevenLabs-compatible AI engine that runs LLMs, vision, voice, image and video models on your own hardware.
summary.what_it_does: LocalAI serves text generation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image, video, embeddings, reranking and object detection models behind one API that mimics OpenAI, Anthropic and ElevenLabs endpoints. Backends (such as llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion, MLX) are separate OCI images pulled on demand when a model needs them. Models can be loaded from the model gallery, Hugging Face, the Ollama registry, YAML configs or standard OCI registries. The README also describes multi-user features (API key auth, quotas, roles), built-in agents with tool use, RAG and MCP, a Realtime speech-to-speech API, distributed mode with PostgreSQL and NATS, and a built-in WebUI. Hardware acceleration is listed for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Apple Silicon Metal, Vulkan and CPU-only. The project also maintains several native C/C++/GGML backends.
use_cases: run open-weight LLMs locally behind an OpenAI-compatible API
generate images or video on your own GPU
swap OpenAI API calls to a private local endpoint
run a multi-user private AI server with API keys and quotas
build RAG or tool-using agents against local models
how_to_run: docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-12  (NVIDIA CUDA 12)
local-ai run llama-3.2-1b-instruct:q4_k_m  (load a model from the gallery)
local-ai run huggingface://TheBloke/phi-2-GGUF/phi-2.Q8_0.gguf  (load a model from Hugging Face)
notable: Modular backends: each engine ships as its own image and is pulled only when a model needs it
Drop-in compatibility with OpenAI, Anthropic and ElevenLabs APIs, plus an Ollama-compatible API per the news section
Native C/C++/GGML backends maintained by the project (e.g. parakeet.cpp, vllm.cpp, face-detect.cpp)
Covers many modalities (LLM, vision, voice, image, video, 3D, detection) behind one API
Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Vulkan or CPU-only hardware
caveats: The macOS DMG is not signed by Apple and needs a quarantine-removal command after install
Feature-rich project with a large surface; the README lists 60+ backends and many optional components that each need their own setup
Some listed features (vllm.cpp) are described as alpha development builds
keywords: private ai on my own hardware
